Those bounded tests establish these examples; they are not a proof for all inputs or a measurement on an iPhone.

Return a canonical String from solve: lowercase true/false for booleans; decimal integers without extra signs, leading zeros or whitespace; comma-separated sequence values and semicolon-separated groups. Whole-number medians have no decimal suffix; half medians use .5. Do not append a newline to the returned value. Preserve the explicitly named textual sentinels such as none or #. Input fixtures are bounded so the demonstrated arithmetic fits its named Rust types; satisfy the stated input preconditions before applying the algorithm.

String and character-grid fixtures use ASCII unless the lesson explicitly specifies Unicode scalar values.

A problem is a good match for Word Break DP when it asks for string segmentation and tokenisation. Here the concrete task is: Return whether the text can be segmented into dictionary words. The visible input `text=leetcode dict=[leet,code]` is an example, not a definition of the whole problem. Ask what operations the solution must support and what the input guarantees. Choose a recurrence when subproblems overlap. `Some` patterns summarize a frontier instead of a full DP table; either representation needs an invariant, and any greedy shortcut needs proof. The right choice follows from those guarantees, not from a familiar noun in the prompt.

The decisive invariant is: Mark a prefix reachable when an earlier reachable prefix is followed by a dictionary word. Try to say why it applies to the task without quoting the implementation. Which fact becomes known after one update, and which possible answers remain? A one-dimensional DP state summarizes a prefix or a single parameter. Define its meaning before writing a recurrence. A counterexample is more useful than a vague warning: change one property of the sample, trace the first two steps, and identify the exact claim that fails.

Compare costs before committing. The advertised bound is O(n * dictionary characters) direct suffix comparisons · O(n) state; identify the operation responsible for it and the extra memory it needs. Then compare a straightforward alternative: a direct scan, full sort, or repeated recomputation may be easier but can pay for the same work many times. Do not choose the more elaborate method just because it has a famous name. For the sample, predict `true` and explain which part of the state lets the method reach that result.

When the prompt is ambiguous, ask about input size, ordering, duplicates, and required output format. Test the base state, the first transition, impossible states, and whether an in-place update accidentally reuses an item twice.
